2026-06-26 Sofia Notes by Gemini
The SEER method (categorize every paragraph by authorial move)
The four authorial moves
Explain: describing, elaborating, giving background or context
Evaluate: the author affirms or criticizes a position or belief
Recommendation: the author proposes a solution or prescription
Comparison: contrasting two competing ideas or theories
Main-point hierarchy: recommendation outranks evaluation outranks comparison outranks explain
The main point is the north star: every other question type is answered in relation to it
Zoom in / zoom out: word to sentence to paragraph to main point
Identifying the author's voice versus a described third-party view
Prephrasing: state what the answer must contain before reading the choices
Inference means must be true
Shopping-list analogy: read for why the author wrote it, not what was written
The test does not reward memorizing content, so orienting on purpose makes you faster and lets you see through the fluff
Boss-proposal analogy: apparent open-mindedness masks a single intended point
Police-interview / hypnosis witness passage drill
Isolated 35-minute RC section under realistic conditions
Blind review
Main-point answers should stay broad and may carry extra detail so long as they nod to the ranking move

With two speakers the main point is the side the author spends more on, not a summary of both
A paragraph's function is read in relation to the whole passage, never in isolation
